title: Water Leisure Safety Act
full_text:
WATER LEISURE SAFETY ACT

Chapter 1 General Provisions

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to ensure safety and order in water leisure activities and promote the sound development of water leisure businesses.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act mean the following:
1. “Water leisure activities” means activities conducted on waters using water leisure craft for hobbies, recreation, sports, education, or similar purposes.
2. “Rafting” means water leisure activities in which a non-power-driven water leisure craft is paddled down rapids or other flows of water in a valley or river.
3. “Water leisure craft” means a vessel or craft used for water leisure activities, classified into power-driven water leisure craft and non-power-driven water leisure craft.
4. “Power-driven water leisure craft” means water leisure craft equipped with a propulsion engine or to which a propulsion engine can readily be attached or from which it can readily be detached, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, including personal watercraft, motorboats, rubber boats, and sailing yachts (meaning yachts equipped with sails and an engine).
5. “Non-power-driven water leisure craft” means water leisure craft other than power-driven water leisure craft, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
6. “Waters” means sea waters and inland waters.
7. “Sea waters” means the flow or surface of water in the sea.
8. “Inland waters” means the flow or surface of fresh water or brackish water in rivers, dams, lakes, swamps, reservoirs, and other artificially created bodies of water.

Article 3 (Exclusions from Application)
(1) This Act does not apply in the following cases:
1. Where a person engages in an excursion ship or ferry business under the Excursion Ship and Ferry Business Act or activities on waters related to that business;
2. Where a person engages in a sports facility business under the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act or activities on waters related to that business;
3. Where a person engages in a fishing vessel business under the Fishing Management and Promotion Act or activities on waters related to that business.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), Articles 16 and 17 shall apply where another Act requires an operator's license under Article 5 as a qualification.

Article 4 (Establishment of Master Plans for Water Leisure Safety Management)
(1) To ensure safety and order in water leisure activities, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall establish and implement a master plan for water leisure safety management (hereinafter referred to as a “master plan”) every 5 years, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) A master plan shall include the following matters:
1. Changes and prospects in the domestic and international policy environment concerning water leisure;
2. Medium- and long-term policy objectives and implementation strategies concerning water leisure, and related matters;
3. Development of the water leisure safety management system;
4. Public-private cooperation for water leisure safety management;
5. Other matters concerning water leisure safety that the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard considers necessary.
(3) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Special Metropolitan City Mayors, Metropolitan City Mayors, Special Self-Governing City Mayors, Do Governors, and Special Self-Governing Province Governors (hereinafter referred to as “Mayors/Do Governors”) of the master plan established under paragraph (1).
(4) A Mayor/Do Governor or the chief of a coast guard station shall establish and implement an annual implementation plan for water leisure safety management (hereinafter referred to as an “implementation plan”) on the basis of the master plan, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(5) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may provide necessary guidance and supervision concerning the establishment and implementation of implementation plans.

Chapter 2 Operator's Licenses

Article 5 (Operator's Licenses)
(1) A person operating a power-driven water leisure craft shall pass the license examination under Article 8 and then obtain a power-driven water leisure craft operator's license from the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard (hereinafter referred to as an “operator's license”).
(2) Operator's licenses shall be classified as follows:
1. General operator's license: Class 1 operator's license and class 2 operator's license;
2. Yacht operator's license.
(3) In the case of general operator's licenses, where a holder of a class 2 operator's license obtains a class 1 operator's license, the class 2 license shall cease to have effect.
(4) Matters necessary for the standards, procedures, methods, and other aspects of operator's licenses shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Special Provisions on Operator's Licenses for Foreign Nationals)
(1) Articles 5 (1) and 25 shall not apply where a foreign national intending to engage in water leisure activities participates in an international sporting competition held in the Republic of Korea and operates a water leisure craft.
(2) Matters necessary for the types of water leisure craft, operating periods and areas, types and scale of international sporting competitions, and other aspects of operation by foreign nationals under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 7 (Disqualifications for Operator's Licenses)
(1) A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs may not obtain an operator's license:
1. A person under 14 years of age (under 18 years of age for a class 1 operator's license); provided, persons falling under Article 9 (1) 1 are excluded;
2. A person prescribed by Presidential Decree among persons with mental illness (meaning persons with mental illness under subparagraph 1 of Article 3 of the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients; hereinafter the same shall apply) who are deemed unable to engage in water leisure activities;
3. A person prescribed by Presidential Decree among persons addicted to narcotics, psychotropic drugs, or cannabis (meaning narcotics, psychotropic drugs, and cannabis under subparagraphs 2 through 4 of Article 2 of the Narcotics Control Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) who are deemed unable to engage in water leisure activities;
4. A person for whom 1 year has not elapsed since revocation of the operator's license under Article 17 (1);
5. A person who has operated a power-driven water leisure craft without obtaining an operator's license in violation of the main clause of the part of Article 25 other than its subparagraphs, and for whom 1 year has not elapsed since the violation (4 years since the violation for a person who, after killing or injuring another person, fled without providing relief or taking other necessary measures).
(2) The heads of institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree among institutions holding personal information shall notify the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard of personal information relevant to disqualifications for operator's licenses.
(3) The contents of personal information to be notified to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard under paragraph (2), the methods of notification, and other matters necessary for notification of personal information shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (License Examinations)
(1) A person intending to obtain an operator's license shall pass an examination administered by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard (hereinafter referred to as a “license examination”).
(2) License examinations shall be conducted separately as written examinations and practical examinations.
(3) A person falling under a disqualification in Article 7 (1) as of the date of the practical examination may not take the license examination.
(4) Matters necessary for the subjects, methods, and other aspects of license examinations shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 9 (Exemptions from License Examinations)
(1) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may exempt a person falling under any of the following subparagraphs from all or part of the subjects of a license examination; provided, a person falling under subparagraph 5 shall be exempt from all subjects of the license examination (limited to class 2 operator's licenses and yacht operator's licenses):
1. A person registered as a power-driven water leisure craft athlete with a sports-related organization prescribed by Presidential Decree;
2. A person satisfying both of the following requirements:
(a) Graduation from a department related to power-driven water leisure craft prescribed by Presidential Decree at a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act (including cases where equivalent academic qualifications are recognized under statutes and regulations);
(b) Completion of subjects concerning power-driven water leisure craft relevant to the license concerned;
3. A person holding a license prescribed by Presidential Decree among maritime officer licenses under the subparagraphs of Article 4 (2) of the Ship Personnel Act;
4. A person who has engaged for at least 1 year in education and training concerning the use of power-driven water leisure craft or related matters at the Sea Explorers of Korea under the Act on the Promotion of the Sea Explorers of Korea or a sports organization under subparagraph 11 of Article 2 of the National Sports Promotion Act, and has been recommended by the head of the organization concerned;
5. A person who has completed education provided by an institution or organization designated and publicly notified by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard (hereinafter referred to as a “license examination exemption education institution”);
6. A person who, after passing the written examination for a class 1 operator's license, intends to switch to and take the practical examination for a class 2 operator's license.
(2) Matters necessary for examination exemption standards under paragraph (1), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) A license examination exemption education institution shall operate the educational curriculum necessary for class 2 operator's license and yacht operator's license education and meet standards for personnel, equipment, facilities, and other resources.
(4) Matters necessary for operation of educational curricula, designation standards concerning personnel, equipment, facilities, and other resources, designation procedures, and other relevant matters for license examination exemption education institutions shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(5) Matters necessary for requirements to be observed by personnel of license examination exemption education institutions, issuance of power-driven water leisure craft operator's license certificates to persons exempted from license examinations, and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 10 (Revocation of Designation of License Examination Exemption Education Institutions)
(1) Where a license examination exemption education institution falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may revoke its designation or suspend its services for a specified period not exceeding 6 months; provided, designation shall be revoked in the case under subparagraph 1:
1. Where designation was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the institution submitted false educational completion results to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, causing a person who had not completed education under Article 9 (1) 5 to be exempted from all license examination subjects;
3. Where the institution failed to comply with the educational curriculum under Article 9 (3);
4. Where the institution ceased to meet the designation standards under Article 9 (4).
(2) Matters necessary for the detailed standards and procedures for revocation of designation and suspension of services of license examination exemption education institutions, and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Sanctions against Persons Engaging in Misconduct)
(1) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may discontinue or invalidate the examination of a person who engages in misconduct in a license examination.
(2) A person whose examination is discontinued or invalidated under paragraph (1) may not take a license examination for 2 years from the date of that disposition.

Article 12 (Renewal of Operator's License Certificates)
(1) A person holding an operator's license shall renew the power-driven water leisure craft operator's license certificate (hereinafter referred to as a “license certificate”) with the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard within the renewal period specified in the following subparagraphs; provided, a person intending to renew a license certificate who cannot renew it within that period due to military service or another reason prescribed by Presidential Decree may renew it in advance or defer renewal, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. The first renewal period shall be within 6 months from the date falling 7 years after issuance of the license certificate;
2. Renewal periods other than that under subparagraph 1 shall be within 6 months from the date falling 7 years after the beginning of the immediately preceding renewal period.
(2) If a license certificate is not renewed under paragraph (1), the operator's license shall be suspended from the day following expiry of the renewal period; provided, where a license certificate is renewed after the operator's license is suspended, the operator's license shall regain effect from the date of renewal.

Article 13 (Water Safety Education)
(1) A person intending to obtain an operator's license shall, after submitting an application for the license examination under Article 8, and a person intending to renew a license certificate shall, within the renewal period under Article 12, receive the following water safety education provided by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard (hereinafter referred to as “safety education”); provided, safety education received before passing the license examination for the first time shall be valid for 6 months, and persons prescribed by Presidential Decree may be exempted from safety education:
1. Statutes and regulations concerning water safety;
2. Matters concerning the use and management of water leisure craft;
3. Other matters necessary for water safety.
(2) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may entrust all or part of the affairs concerning safety education to an institution or organization designated by the Commissioner (hereinafter referred to as an “entrusted safety education institution”).
(3) Matters necessary for designation standards concerning personnel, equipment, facilities, and other resources, and designation procedures for entrusted safety education institutions shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Revocation of Designation of Entrusted Safety Education Institutions)
(1) Where an entrusted safety education institution falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may revoke its designation or suspend its services for a specified period not exceeding 6 months; provided, designation shall be revoked in the case under subparagraph 1:
1. Where designation was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where a certificate of completion of safety education was issued by fraud or other improper means;
3. Where the institution ceased to meet the designation standards under Article 13 (3).
(2) Matters necessary for the detailed standards and procedures for revocation of designation and suspension of services of entrusted safety education institutions, and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Issuance of License Certificates)
(1) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall issue a license certificate in either of the following cases:
1. Where a license certificate is issued upon passing the license examination under Article 8 (1);
2. Where a license certificate is renewed under Article 12.
(2) An operator's license takes effect when the license certificate is issued to the holder or the holder's agent under paragraph (1).
(3) If a license certificate is lost or becomes worn and unusable, its holder may report this to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard and obtain a replacement.
(4) Matters necessary for procedures for issuance and reissuance of license certificates under paragraphs (1) and (3), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 16 (Duty to Carry License Certificates)
(1) A person operating a power-driven water leisure craft shall carry the license certificate.
(2) An operator under paragraph (1) shall produce the license certificate if requested by a relevant public official during operation.
(3) No person shall borrow or lend a license certificate or arrange such borrowing or lending.

Article 17 (Revocation and Suspension of Operator's Licenses)
(1) Where a person holding an operator's license falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may revoke the license or suspend it for a specified period not exceeding 1 year, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; provided, the license shall be revoked in a case under subparagraph 1, 2, or any of subparagraphs 4 through 6. <Amended December 20, 2024>
1. Where the person obtained an operator's license by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the person operated a craft during suspension of the operator's license;
3. Where the license holder used a power-driven water leisure craft to commit a crime prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, such as murder or robbery;
4. Where the person came to fall under a disqualification for an operator's license under Article 7 (1) 2 or 3;
5. Where a person disqualified from obtaining an operator's license under Article 7 (1) obtained such a license;
6. Where, in violation of Article 27 (1) or (2), the person operated a craft while intoxicated, or failed to comply with testing by a relevant public official despite reasonable grounds to believe that the person was intoxicated (limited to operation of a power-driven water leisure craft);
7. Where, during operation, the person intentionally or negligently killed or injured another person or caused serious damage to another person's property;
8. Where the person lent the license certificate to another person to operate a craft;
9. Where the person operated a power-driven water leisure craft while likely to be unable to operate normally due to the influence of drugs, in violation of Article 28;
10. Where the person otherwise violated this Act or an order under this Act for maintaining safety and order in water leisure activities.
(2) A person whose operator's license is revoked or suspended under paragraph (1) shall return the license certificate to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard within 7 days from the date of revocation or suspension.

Article 18 (Performance of License Examination Services by Agencies)
(1) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may have an institution or organization designated by the Commissioner (hereinafter referred to as an “examination agency”) perform all or part of the services relating to license examinations on the Commissioner's behalf.
(2) Where an examination agency falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may revoke its designation or suspend its services for a period not exceeding 6 months; provided, designation shall be revoked in the case under subparagraph 1 or 2:
1. Where designation was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the head, responsible operator, or personnel of the examination agency engaged in misconduct in relation to license examinations (including cases of instructing or tolerating such misconduct);
3. Where the agency ceased to meet the designation standards under paragraph (5);
4. Where grounds arose preventing the agency from properly performing license examination services under this Act or orders issued under this Act.
(3) An examination agency shall report to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard on license examination services performed on the Commissioner's behalf under paragraph (1).
(4) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall verify the handling of license examination services reported under paragraph (3), and may take necessary measures if a violation of this Act or an order issued under this Act is found.
(5) Matters necessary for performance of license examination services by agencies and designation standards for examination agencies under paragraph (1), procedures for revocation and suspension of designation under paragraph (2), reports under paragraph (3), supervision of examination agencies under paragraph (4), and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Training of Personnel)
(1) Persons engaged in examination or education services at license examination exemption education institutions, entrusted safety education institutions, or examination agencies shall receive training provided by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard.
(2) Matters necessary for the timing, persons subject to, methods, and other aspects of training under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Chapter 3 Safety Obligations

Article 20 (Wearing Safety Equipment)
A person engaging in water leisure activities shall wear equipment necessary for the safety of human life, such as a life jacket, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 21 (Compliance with Operating Rules)
A person engaging in water leisure activities shall comply with matters concerning operating methods, craft speed, operating areas under Article 16 (2) of the Act on the Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft, and other relevant matters, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 22 (Restrictions on Water Leisure Activities due to Weather)
No person shall engage in water leisure activities where the intended area falls under either of the following subparagraphs; provided, this shall not apply in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of the characteristics of water leisure craft powered solely by waves or wind:
1. Where a special weather report at the advisory level or higher is in effect for a typhoon, high seas, storm surge, heavy rain, heavy snow, or strong wind;
2. Where visibility is limited to 0.5 kilometers or less due to fog or another cause.

Article 23 (Reporting Long-Distance Water Leisure Activities)
(1) A person intending to engage in water leisure activities at a location 10 nautical miles or more from the port of departure shall report to a coast guard or police authority, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; provided, this shall not apply to a vessel that has reported its entry or departure under Article 4 of the Act on the Arrival and Departure of Ships or reported departure or arrival under Article 15 of the Rules on Safe Vessel Operations.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), no person shall engage in water leisure activities 10 nautical miles or more from the port of departure using a craft other than a power-driven water leisure craft under Article 3 of the Act on the Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft (hereinafter referred to as a “power-driven water leisure craft subject to registration”); provided, this shall not apply in cases prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, such as accompaniment by a safety management vessel or formation of a flotilla.

Article 24 (Reporting Accidents)
(1) A person engaging in water leisure activities shall, in any of the following cases, report without delay to a relevant administrative agency, such as a coast guard, police, or fire authority, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries:
1. Where a person accompanying the operator on a water leisure craft dies, goes missing, or suffers a serious injury due to an accident;
2. Where a collision, grounding, or other accident affecting or likely to affect safe operation of a water leisure craft occurs.
(2) The head of the relevant administrative agency receiving a report under paragraph (1) shall take necessary measures for lifesaving, handling the accident, and other relevant purposes.
(3) After taking necessary measures under paragraph (2), the chief of a police station or fire station receiving a report under paragraph (1) shall notify the chief of the competent coast guard station if the accident occurred in sea waters, or the competent Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu if it occurred in inland waters (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu, and, in the case of the Han River within the jurisdiction of Seoul Special Metropolitan City, means the head of the agency responsible for managing the Han River in Seoul Special Metropolitan City; hereinafter referred to as “head of a Si/Gun/Gu”), of the results.

Article 25 (Prohibition of Unlicensed Operation)
No person shall operate a power-driven water leisure craft requiring an operator's license without obtaining that license (including cases where the license is suspended); provided, this shall not apply in either of the following cases:
1. Where the person engages in water leisure activities under the supervision of a holder of a class 1 operator's license, in a case prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries;
2. Where the person operates a craft while accompanied on board by a holder of an operator's license, in a case prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 26 (Prohibition of Water Leisure Activities at Night)
(1) No person shall engage in water leisure activities from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise; provided, this shall not apply where a water leisure craft equipped with night navigation equipment is used as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) If considered necessary, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may adjust the hours under the main clause of paragraph (1) for a specified area, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(3) Where hours are adjusted under paragraph (2), the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall publicly announce that fact in a place easily visible to persons engaging in water leisure activities.

Article 27 (Prohibition of Operation While Intoxicated)
(1) No person shall operate a water leisure craft while intoxicated (meaning the state of intoxication under Article 39 (4) of the Maritime Traffic Safety Act; hereinafter the same shall apply). <Amended July 25, 2023; December 20, 2024>
(2) A person falling under either of the following subparagraphs (hereinafter referred to as a “relevant public official”) may test a person who has operated a water leisure craft for intoxication where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the person violated paragraph (1). In such cases, the person who operated the craft shall comply with the test. <Amended December 20, 2024>
1. A police official;
2. A public official belonging to a Si/Gun/Gu who performs water leisure safety duties.
(3) When conducting a test for intoxication under paragraph (2), a relevant public official (excluding a police official in uniform) shall carry identification indicating the official's authority and present it to the person who operated the water leisure craft. <Amended December 20, 2024>
(4) A person who objects to the result of a test for intoxication under paragraph (2) may, with that person's consent, be tested again by taking a blood sample or another method.

Article 28 (Prohibition of Operation under the Influence of Drugs or Other Substances)
No person shall operate a water leisure craft while likely to be unable to operate normally due to the influence of narcotics, psychotropic drugs, or cannabis under Article 2 of the Narcotics Control Act, hallucinogenic substances under Article 22 of the Chemicals Control Act, or another cause. <Amended December 20, 2024>

Article 29 (Prohibition of Exceeding Passenger Capacity)
No person shall operate a water leisure craft with more persons on board than its capacity, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Chapter 4 Safety Management

Article 30 (Designation of Areas Prohibited for Water Leisure Activities)
(1) If considered necessary for the safety of water leisure activities, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may designate areas prohibited for water leisure activities (including areas prohibited for particular types of water leisure craft).
(2) No person shall engage in water leisure activities in a prohibited area designated under paragraph (1).

Article 31 (Corrective Orders)
If considered necessary for the safety of water leisure activities, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may order a person engaging in or intending to engage in water leisure activities to take any of the following measures; provided, corrective orders to a person intending to engage in water leisure activities shall be limited to cases where an accident is clearly foreseeable:
1. Limitation of the number of persons riding a water leisure craft (including persons pushed or towed by the craft; hereinafter the same shall apply), or replacement of the operator;
2. Temporary suspension of water leisure activities;
3. Improvement or replacement of the water leisure craft.

Article 32 (Stopping and Checking Craft)
(1) Where a relevant public official considers that a person riding a water leisure craft has violated this Act or an order issued under this Act, the official may stop the craft to check the matter or require the person engaging in water leisure activities to produce a license certificate or identification document.
(2) When stopping a water leisure craft and requiring production of a license certificate or another document under paragraph (1), the relevant public official shall carry identification indicating the official's authority and present it to the person concerned.

Article 33 (Cooperation of Relevant Administrative Agencies)
(1) If considered necessary for the safety of water leisure activities, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, commissioner of a regional coast guard headquarters, chief of a coast guard station, Mayor/Do Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu may request cooperation from the head of a relevant administrative agency. In such cases, the head of the relevant administrative agency receiving the request shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(2) If considered necessary for efficient safety management of water leisure activities in inland waters under the jurisdiction concerned, a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may request the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, commissioner of a regional coast guard headquarters, or chief of a coast guard station to dispatch relevant police officials or undertake safety management duties for water leisure activities in a specified area. In such cases, the Commissioner, regional commissioner, or station chief receiving the request shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 34 (Establishment of the Korea Water Leisure Safety Association)
(1) The Korea Water Leisure Safety Association (hereinafter referred to as the “Association”) may be established to perform services entrusted by administrative agencies, including the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, such as research and development, publicity, education, and training concerning safety management of water leisure activities, to promote the sound development of the water leisure industry, and to improve the safety management capabilities of personnel involved in water leisure.
(2) The Association shall be a corporation.
(3) The Association shall conduct the following activities:
1. Research projects to promote water leisure safety and the water leisure industry;
2. Research projects to develop operator's license examination management systems and water leisure craft registration systems;
3. Performance on behalf of the authorities of operator's license examinations and the registration, safety inspection, and safety checks of water leisure craft;
4. Lifesaving education and water safety education for water leisure business operators, participants in water leisure activities, and others, and development of related equipment and teaching materials;
5. Services entrusted by the State or a local government under this Act or other statutes and regulations;
6. Other activities considered necessary by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard.
(4) Where considered necessary, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may provide financial support to the Association within the budget to facilitate its performance of the activities under paragraph (3).
(5) Matters necessary for the Association's articles of incorporation, affairs, membership qualifications, supervision, and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(6) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated associations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Association.

Article 35 (Operation of Water Leisure Activity Safety Councils)
(1) A Mayor/Do Governor may establish and operate a water leisure activity safety council consisting of representatives of relevant administrative agencies, organizations, and other bodies with jurisdiction over the region concerned, to establish a cooperative framework for efficient safety management of water leisure activities.
(2) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of a water leisure activity safety council under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by ordinance of the relevant local government, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may request a Mayor/Do Governor to establish and operate a water leisure activity safety council for the safety management of water leisure activities. In such cases, the Mayor/Do Governor receiving the request shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 36 (Establishment and Operation of Computerized Systems)
(1) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may establish and operate a comprehensive water leisure information system for systematic safety management of water leisure activities.
(2) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may handle affairs prescribed in this Act or the Act on the Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft through the comprehensive water leisure information system, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Chapter 5 Water Leisure Businesses

Article 37 (Registration of Water Leisure Businesses)
(1) A person intending to operate a business of renting water leisure craft or carrying persons engaging in water leisure activities on water leisure craft (hereinafter referred to as a “water leisure business”) shall register matters concerning permission to occupy or use rivers or other public waters, and other relevant matters, with the authority classified in the following subparagraphs. In such cases, registration standards may be relaxed for a water leisure business operator intending to operate a craft rental business, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
1. Where the business area is in sea waters: The chief of the coast guard station having jurisdiction over the area;
2. Where the business area is in inland waters: The head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the area;
3. Where the business area spans areas under the jurisdiction of two or more coast guard station chiefs or heads of Sis/Guns/Gus: The chief of the coast guard station or head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the place where the water leisure craft used for the business are mainly moored.
(2) A water leisure business operator registered under paragraph (1) shall register changes to registered matters, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(3) Before making a registration upon an application for registration or registration of a change under paragraph (1) or (2), the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall consult with other coast guard station chiefs or heads of Sis/Guns/Gus having jurisdiction over the business area concerned.
(4) Matters necessary for registration of water leisure businesses, including registration standards, procedures, and adjustment of business areas under paragraph (1), shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 38 (Validity Period of Business Registration)
(1) Registration of a water leisure business under Article 37 (1) shall be valid for 10 years; provided, where the intended business period is less than 10 years, that business period shall be the registration validity period.
(2) A person intending to continue a water leisure business after expiry of the registration validity period under paragraph (1) shall renew the registration, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 39 (Disqualifications for Registration of Water Leisure Businesses)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs may not register a water leisure business:
1. A minor, person under adult guardianship, or person under limited guardianship;
2. A person sentenced to imprisonment or a heavier punishment for violating this Act, for whom 2 years have not elapsed since completion of execution of the sentence or exemption from its execution;
3. A person sentenced to imprisonment or a heavier punishment with suspension of execution for violating this Act, who is still within the suspension period;
4. A person for whom 2 years have not elapsed since revocation of registration under Article 48 (excluding revocation on a ground under subparagraph 1 of this Article).

Article 40 (Succession to Rights and Obligations)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall succeed to the rights and obligations of a water leisure business operator arising from registration of the business:
1. The heir, where a water leisure business operator dies;
2. The transferee, where a water leisure business operator transfers the business;
3. The corporation surviving a merger or newly established through a merger, where a water leisure business operator that is a corporation merges.

Article 41 (Reports of Suspension and Other Changes in Business)
(1) A water leisure business operator intending to suspend or discontinue the business during the registered business period shall report to the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) A water leisure business operator intending to reopen a suspended water leisure business shall report to the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. In such cases, the coast guard station chief or head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall review the report and accept it if it complies with this Act.
(3) The chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu receiving a report of suspension, discontinuance, or reopening under paragraph (1) or (2) shall notify the tax office having jurisdiction over the location of the water leisure business establishment of that fact.

Article 42 (User Charges)
Where a water leisure business operator determines user charges, such as boarding fees or rental fees, the operator shall report them to the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, and then post them in a clearly visible place within the business establishment. The same shall apply to changes to reported matters.

Article 43 (Safety Checks)
(1) For the safety of water leisure activities, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall have relevant public officials conduct safety checks of water leisure craft and water leisure facilities, such as landing stages, and may disclose the results.
(2) On the basis of the results of a safety check under paragraph (1), the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may order maintenance or restoration to the original condition, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. In such cases, the authority may also order suspension of use of the water leisure craft concerned for a specified period necessary for maintenance or restoration.
(3) A public official conducting a check under paragraph (1) shall carry identification indicating the official's authority and present it to persons concerned.
(4) Matters necessary for the subjects, items, timing, procedures, disclosure of results, and other aspects of safety checks under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 44 (Safety Checks and Other Measures by Business Operators)
(1) A water leisure business operator and its personnel shall take the following measures for the safety of water leisure activities:
1. Safety checks of water leisure craft and facilities;
2. Checking weather and water conditions in the business area;
3. Relief measures and notification to relevant administrative agencies, such as coast guard, police, and fire authorities, if an accident occurs in the business area;
4. Ensuring that users wear safety equipment and providing safety education before boarding;
5. Deployment of lifesaving personnel or rafting guides at the business establishment, or having them on board;
6. Deployment of an emergency rescue boat (meaning a power-driven water leisure craft used for patrols of the water leisure business establishment and its business area and for lifesaving; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article).
(2) A water leisure business operator and its personnel shall not engage in any of the following acts in the business area:
1. Allowing a person under 14 years of age (limited to persons unaccompanied by a guardian), an intoxicated person, or a person with mental illness to board a water leisure craft, or renting a craft to such a person;
2. Allowing more persons to board a water leisure craft than its capacity;
3. Selling or providing alcoholic beverages on a water leisure craft, or allowing users to bring them on board;
4. Conducting business outside the business area;
5. Conducting business outside the hours for water leisure activities under Article 26;
6. Bringing onto or transporting on a water leisure craft carrying users dangerous substances prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as explosives or flammable substances;
7. Using for business a power-driven water leisure craft that has not undergone a safety inspection under Article 15 of the Act on the Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft;
8. Using an emergency rescue boat for a purpose other than its intended purpose.
(3) Qualifications and deployment standards for lifesaving personnel or rafting guides under paragraph (1) 5, matters necessary for deployment of emergency rescue boats under paragraph (1) 6, and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 45 (Requirements for Operators of Water Leisure Craft Not Subject to Registration)
Water leisure business operators operating craft other than power-driven water leisure craft subject to registration, and their personnel, shall comply with matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries concerning operation of the craft, safety standards, and related matters.

Article 46 (Restrictions on Business)
(1) In any of the following cases, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may order a water leisure business operator to limit the business area or hours, or temporarily suspend business; provided, in the cases under subparagraphs 3 through 5, such an order may be issued only for business activities using water leisure craft prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as craft on which the user's body directly contacts the water surface:
1. Where weather or water conditions deteriorate;
2. Where an accident on waters occurs;
3. Where water quality is polluted by leakage of oil, chemicals, or similar substances, or the occurrence of green algae, red tides, or similar phenomena;
4. Where obstacles such as floating matter occur;
5. Where harmful organisms capable of harming the human body or life occur;
6. Where another ground prescribed by Presidential Decree arises.
(2) Where the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu determines that a ground under a subparagraph of paragraph (1) has ceased or has been alleviated, the authority shall lift the restriction on the business area or hours, or the temporary suspension of business.

Article 47 (Submission of Materials)
If considered necessary for the safety of water leisure activities, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may require a water leisure business operator to submit relevant documents or materials, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 48 (Revocation of Registration of Water Leisure Businesses)
Where a water leisure business operator falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may revoke registration of the business or order suspension of all or part of the business for a period not exceeding 3 months, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; provided, registration shall be revoked in the cases under subparagraphs 1 through 3:
1. Where registration was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where the operator comes to fall under any subparagraph of Article 39;
3. Where the operator continues the business after expiry of permission to occupy or use public waters;
4. Where the business operator or its personnel intentionally or negligently kill or injure a person;
5. Where the operator uses for the business a water leisure craft in violation of Article 6, 9, 10, 13, 15, or 17 of the Act on the Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft;
6. Where the operator fails to register a change under Article 37 (2);
7. Where the operator violates Articles 42 through 46, Article 49 (2), or Article 50, or an order under those provisions.

Chapter 6 Insurance

Article 49 (Enrollment in Insurance or Mutual Aid)
(1) The owner of a power-driven water leisure craft subject to registration shall, within 1 month from becoming its owner, enroll in insurance or mutual aid (hereinafter referred to as “insurance or mutual aid”), as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to compensate a victim (where the victim dies, meaning the person entitled to damages) if another person dies or is injured through use of the craft.
(2) A water leisure business operator shall enroll in insurance or mutual aid to cover harm suffered by its personnel and users, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 50 (Provision of Information on Enrollment in Insurance or Mutual Aid)
A water leisure business operator shall inform its personnel and users of information concerning enrollment in insurance or mutual aid under Article 49, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 51 (Requests for Insurance or Mutual Aid Enrollment Information)
(1) To investigate and manage enrollment in insurance or mutual aid under Article 49, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, commissioner of a regional coast guard headquarters, chief of a coast guard station, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu may request insurance companies and mutual aid providers (hereinafter referred to as “insurance companies and similar entities”), or insurance associations and similar bodies under Chapter 11, Section 1 of the Insurance Business Act (hereinafter referred to as “insurance associations and similar bodies”), to provide materials or information necessary for investigation and management of enrollment.
(2) Where requested to provide materials or information under paragraph (1), insurance companies and similar entities may provide them through insurance associations and similar bodies.
(3) A person requested to provide materials or information under paragraph (1) shall comply unless there are justifiable grounds not to do so.

Article 52 (Establishment and Operation of an Insurance or Mutual Aid Enrollment Management Network)
(1) For efficient performance of insurance or mutual aid enrollment management duties, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may establish and operate an insurance or mutual aid enrollment management network (hereinafter referred to as the “enrollment management network”) by linking the comprehensive water leisure information system under Article 36 (1) with computerized systems managed and operated by insurance companies and similar entities or insurance associations and similar bodies, or similar computerized systems.
(2) For establishment and operation of the enrollment management network, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may request insurance companies and similar entities or insurance associations and similar bodies to provide information prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, a person requested to provide relevant information shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(3) Matters necessary for operation of the enrollment management network shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 53 (Measures concerning Persons without Insurance or Mutual Aid)
(1) Where a person required to enroll in insurance or mutual aid falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the insurance company or similar entity shall notify the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, commissioner of a regional coast guard headquarters, chief of a coast guard station, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu of that fact within the period prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries:
1. Where the person enters into an insurance or mutual aid contract with that entity;
2. Where the person terminates an insurance or mutual aid contract with that entity before expiry of the contract period;
3. Where a person who entered into an insurance or mutual aid contract with that entity fails to enter into a new contract after expiry of the contract period.
(2) Upon receiving a notification under paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, commissioner of a regional coast guard headquarters, chief of a coast guard station, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall, without delay, order a person required to enroll but not enrolled in insurance or mutual aid to enroll and submit documents proving enrollment within a specified period of at least 10 days and not more than 15 days.

Article 54 (Prohibition of Registration and Other Dispositions for Persons without Insurance or Mutual Aid)
(1) In any of the following cases, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, commissioner of a regional coast guard headquarters, chief of a coast guard station, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall verify whether the person required to enroll under Article 49 is enrolled in insurance or mutual aid and accept the registration application or report only if enrollment is confirmed:
1. Where the owner of a power-driven water leisure craft subject to registration applies for registration of a craft subject to mandatory insurance or mutual aid under Articles 6 (1) and 9 of the Act on the Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft;
2. Where a water leisure business operator applies for registration of a water leisure business or reports reopening under Article 37 or Article 41 (2).
(2) Matters necessary for methods and procedures for confirming insurance or mutual aid enrollment under paragraph (1), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 55 (Entrustment of Authority)
The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may entrust duties concerning establishment and operation of the enrollment management network to insurance companies and similar entities or insurance associations and similar bodies.

Chapter 7 Supplementary Provisions

Article 56 (Penalty Surcharges)
(1) Where a license examination exemption education institution, entrusted safety education institution, or examination agency falls under a ground in the following classifications requiring suspension of services, and the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard considers that suspension would cause serious inconvenience to users of the institution or otherwise be likely to harm the public interest, the Commissioner may impose a penalty surcharge not exceeding 10 million won in lieu of suspension of services:
1. License examination exemption education institution: Article 10 (1) 2 through 4;
2. Entrusted safety education institution: Article 14 (1) 2 and 3;
3. Examination agency: Article 18 (2) 3 and 4.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where a license examination exemption education institution, entrusted safety education institution, or examination agency has been subject to a disposition imposing a penalty surcharge under paragraph (1) and again commits a violation subject to a penalty surcharge within 2 years from the date of that disposition, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall order suspension of services.
(3) The types of violations for which penalty surcharges are imposed under paragraph (1), the amounts of penalty surcharges according to the severity of violations, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) If a license examination exemption education institution, entrusted safety education institution, or examination agency fails to pay a penalty surcharge under paragraph (1) by the payment deadline, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall collect it in the same manner as compulsory collection of national taxes.

Article 57 (Fees)
(1) A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall pay a fee to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries:
1. A person intending to take a license examination under Article 8 (1);
2. A person intending to receive safety education under Article 13 (1);
3. A person intending to apply for issuance, reissuance, or renewal of a license certificate under Article 15;
4. A person intending to apply for registration or registration of a change to a water leisure business, or to report suspension, discontinuance, reopening, or related matters under Articles 37 and 41.
(2) In either of the following cases, fees determined by the entrusted safety education institution or examination agency shall be paid to the agency or institution concerned:
1. Where safety education is entrusted under Article 13 (2);
2. Where an examination agency performs license examination services under Article 18 (1).
(3) An entrusted safety education institution or examination agency shall obtain approval from the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard when determining or changing fees under paragraph (2).
(4) Revenue from fees collected under paragraph (2) by an entrusted safety education institution or examination agency shall be revenue of that institution or agency.
(5) Matters necessary for standards for refunding fees paid to take a license examination or receive safety education under paragraph (1) 1 and 2, and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 58 (Hearings)
(1) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall hold a hearing before making any of the following dispositions:
1. Revocation of designation or suspension of services of a license examination exemption education institution under Article 10 (1), or imposition of a penalty surcharge under Article 56 (1) 1;
2. Revocation of designation or suspension of services of an entrusted safety education institution under Article 14 (1), or imposition of a penalty surcharge under Article 56 (1) 2;
3. Revocation of designation or suspension of services of an examination agency under Article 18 (2), or imposition of a penalty surcharge under Article 56 (1) 3.
(2) The chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall hold a hearing before revoking registration of a water leisure business under Article 48.

Article 59 (Delegation of Authority)
Part of the authority of the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard under this Act may be delegated to the heads of the Commissioner's subordinate agencies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 60 (Deemed Public Officials for Application of Penalty Provisions)
Executives and employees of license examination exemption education institutions, entrusted safety education institutions, and examination agencies, and executives and employees of insurance companies and similar entities or insurance associations and similar bodies engaged in duties entrusted under Article 55, shall be deemed public officials for purposes of the penalties under Articles 127 and 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Chapter 8 Penalty Provisions

Article 61 (Penalties)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 1 year or a fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Amended December 20, 2024>
1. A person who borrows or lends a license certificate or arranges such borrowing or lending, in violation of Article 16 (3);
2. A person who operates a power-driven water leisure craft without obtaining an operator's license, in violation of the main clause of the part of Article 25 other than its subparagraphs;
3. A person who operates a power-driven water leisure craft while intoxicated, in violation of Article 27 (1);
4. A person who fails to comply with testing by a relevant public official under Article 27 (2), despite reasonable grounds to believe that the person is intoxicated (limited to a person who operated a power-driven water leisure craft);
5. A person who operates a power-driven water leisure craft while likely to be unable to operate normally due to drug use or another cause, in violation of Article 28;
6. A person who conducts a water leisure business without registration or registration of a change, in violation of Article 37 (1) and (2);
7. A person who conducts a water leisure business after revocation of its registration or during suspension of business under Article 48.

Article 62 (Penalties)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 6 months or a fine not exceeding 5 million won:
1. A water leisure business operator who violates an order for maintenance or restoration to the original condition under Article 43 (2);
2. A water leisure business operator or its personnel who fail to take measures necessary for safety or engage in a prohibited act, in violation of Article 44;
3. A water leisure business operator who violates an order restricting the business area or hours or temporarily suspending business under Article 46.

Article 63 (Joint Penalty Provisions)
If a representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation or individual, commits any violation under Article 61 or 62 in connection with the business of the corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall, in addition to punishment of the offender, be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article; provided, this shall not apply where the corporation or individual has exercised due care and supervision over the business concerned to prevent the violation.

Article 64 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 1 million won. <Amended December 20, 2024>
1. A person who fails to receive training in violation of Article 19 (1);
2. A person who engages in water leisure activities outside the hours under Article 26 (1) and (2);
2-2. A person who operates a non-power-driven water leisure craft while intoxicated, in violation of Article 27 (1);
2-3. A person who fails to comply with testing by a relevant public official under Article 27 (2), despite reasonable grounds to believe that the person is intoxicated (limited to a person who operated a non-power-driven water leisure craft);
2-4. A person who operates a non-power-driven water leisure craft while likely to be unable to operate normally due to drug use or another cause, in violation of Article 28;
3. A person who operates a craft with more persons than its capacity, in violation of Article 29;
4. A person who engages in water leisure activities in a prohibited area, in violation of Article 30 (2);
5. A water leisure business operator who fails to report suspension, discontinuance, or reopening, in violation of Article 41 (1) and (2);
6. A water leisure business operator who receives money or valuables other than the user charges reported under Article 42, or fails to post reported matters;
7. A water leisure business operator or its personnel who violate the requirements for operators of craft not subject to registration under Article 45;
8. A water leisure business operator who fails to submit documents or materials under Article 47, or submits false documents or materials;
9. A water leisure business operator who fails to enroll in insurance or mutual aid, in violation of Article 49 (2);
10. A water leisure business operator who, without justifiable grounds, fails to provide information on enrollment in insurance or mutual aid or provides false information, in violation of Article 50;
11. An insurance company or similar entity that fails to give notification, in violation of Article 53 (1).
(2) A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 500,000 won:
1. A person who fails to return a license certificate, in violation of Article 17 (2);
2. A person who fails to wear lifesaving equipment, in violation of Article 20;
3. A person who fails to comply with operating rules or related requirements, in violation of Article 21;
4. A person who engages in water leisure activities in an area where such activities are restricted due to weather, in violation of Article 22;
5. A person who fails to report long-distance water leisure activities, in violation of Article 23 (1);
6. A person who engages in water leisure activities 10 nautical miles or more from the port of departure using a craft not subject to registration, in violation of Article 23 (2);
7. A person who fails to report an accident, in violation of Article 24 (1);
8. A person who fails to comply with a corrective order under Article 31;
9. A person who refuses an order to stop temporarily or produce a license certificate or identification document under Article 32;
10. A person who fails to enroll in insurance or mutual aid, in violation of Article 49 (1).
(3) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be imposed and collected, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, commissioner of a regional coast guard headquarters, or chief of a coast guard station in the case of sea waters, and by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu in the case of inland waters.
(4) Procedures concerning imposition and collection, trial, enforcement, and other aspects of administrative fines under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be governed by the Act on the Regulation of Violations of Public Order.

ADDENDA <Act No. 18958, June 10, 2022>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date on which 1 year has elapsed after its promulgation; provided, Articles 52 through 55 and the portions concerning insurance companies and similar entities and insurance associations and similar bodies in the amended provisions of Article 60 shall enter into force on the date on which 3 years have elapsed after promulgation.

Article 2 (Application concerning Disqualifications for Operator's Licenses)
The amended provisions of Article 7 of this Act shall apply where a ground for disqualification for an operator's license under Article 5 (1) 4 or 5 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act exists as at the time this Act enters into force.

Article 3 (Application concerning Revocation and Suspension of Operator's Licenses)
The amended provisions of Article 17 of this Act shall apply where a ground for revocation or suspension of an operator's license under Article 13 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act exists as at the time this Act enters into force.

Article 4 (Application concerning Disqualifications for Registration of Water Leisure Businesses)
The amended provisions of Article 39 of this Act shall apply to disqualifications for registration of a water leisure business concerning a person who has been or is being punished for a violation of the former Water Leisure Safety Act, or whose registration has been revoked, as at the time this Act enters into force.

Article 5 (Application concerning Disclosure of Safety Check Results)
Disclosure of safety check results under Article 43 (1) shall begin to apply to safety checks conducted after this Act enters into force.

Article 6 (General Transitional Measures)
Dispositions, procedures, and other acts performed under the former provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall, where this Act contains corresponding provisions, be deemed performed under those provisions of this Act.

Article 7 (Transitional Measures concerning Operator's Licenses and Safety Education)
(1) A person who has obtained an operator's license under the former provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed to hold an operator's license under Article 5 of this Act until expiry of that license's validity period.
(2) A person who, under the former provisions, is under 18 years of age and holds a class 1 operator's license as at the time this Act enters into force shall, notwithstanding the amended provisions of Article 7 (1) 1, be deemed to have validly obtained a class 1 operator's license under the former provisions.
(3) A person who has received safety education under the former provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed to have received safety education under the amended provisions of Article 13 of this Act.

Article 8 (Transitional Measures concerning Designation of License Examination Exemption Education Institutions)
A license examination exemption education institution designated under the former provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed designated under the amended provisions of Article 9.

Article 9 (Transitional Measures concerning Designation of Entrusted Safety Education Institutions)
An entrusted safety education institution designated under the former provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed designated under the amended provisions of Article 13.

Article 10 (Transitional Measures concerning Designation of Examination Agencies)
An agency designated to perform license examination services under the former provisions as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed designated under the amended provisions of Article 18.

Article 11 (Transitional Measures concerning Prohibited Acts)
Where, as at the time this Act enters into force, a person has operated without a license, engaged in water leisure activities at night, operated while intoxicated, operated under the influence of drugs or similar substances, or carried persons in excess of capacity, in violation of Articles 20 through 24 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act, the person shall be deemed to have committed a violation under the amended provisions of Articles 25 through 29.

Article 12 (Transitional Measures concerning the Korea Water Leisure Safety Association)
The Korea Water Leisure Safety Association established under Article 28-2 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed the Korea Water Leisure Safety Association established under Article 34 of this Act.

Article 13 (Transitional Measures concerning Water Leisure Activity Safety Councils)
A water leisure activity safety council established under Article 29 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed a council established under Article 35 of this Act.

Article 14 (Transitional Measures concerning Registration of Water Leisure Businesses)
Registration and related procedures undertaken under the former provisions by a person intending to operate a water leisure business as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed undertaken under the amended provisions of Article 37.

Article 15 (Transitional Measures concerning Business Registration Validity Periods)
A person who has registered a business under Article 39-3 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed registered under Article 38 of this Act until expiry of that business registration's validity period.

Article 16 (Transitional Measures concerning Succession to Rights and Obligations)
Matters concerning succession to rights and obligations under Article 41 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed matters concerning succession to rights and obligations under Article 40 of this Act.

Article 17 (Transitional Measures concerning Revocation of Registration of Water Leisure Businesses)
Matters concerning revocation of registration of water leisure businesses and related matters under Article 51 of the former Water Leisure Safety Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed matters under Article 48 of this Act.

Article 18 (Transitional Measures concerning Applications, Reports, and Notifications)
Applications, reports, notifications, and similar acts under the former Water Leisure Safety Act as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed applications, reports, notifications, and similar acts under this Act.

Article 19 (Transitional Measures concerning Fees)
Application of provisions on fees to acts requiring payment of a fee before this Act enters into force shall be governed by the former provisions.

Article 20 (Transitional Measures concerning Administrative Dispositions and Penalty Surcharges)
Application of provisions on administrative dispositions and penalty surcharges to violations committed before this Act enters into force shall be governed by the former provisions.

Article 21 (Transitional Measures concerning Penalties and Administrative Fines)
Application of provisions on penalties and administrative fines to violations committed before this Act enters into force shall be governed by the former provisions.

Article 22 (Amendment of Other Acts)
(1) The Act on the Development and Management of Marinas is partially amended as follows:
In Article 28-5 (2) 6, “Article 39 of the Water Leisure Safety Act” is replaced with “Article 37 of the Water Leisure Safety Act”.
(2) The Industrial Standardization Act is partially amended as follows:
Subparagraph 17 of Article 26 is deleted.
(3) The Act on Search and Rescue on Waters is partially amended as follows:
In Article 2, subparagraph 2, “Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the Water Leisure Safety Act” is replaced with “Article 2, subparagraph 7 of the Water Leisure Safety Act”; in subparagraph 3 of the same Article, “Article 2, subparagraph 7 of the Water Leisure Safety Act” is replaced with “Article 2, subparagraph 8 of the Water Leisure Safety Act”.
(4) The Act on Safety and Promotion of Underwater Leisure Activities is partially amended as follows:
In Article 2, subparagraph 1, “Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the Water Leisure Safety Act” is replaced with “Article 2, subparagraph 7 of the Water Leisure Safety Act”, and “subparagraph 7 of the same Article” is replaced with “subparagraph 8 of the same Article”.
(5) The Youth Activity Promotion Act is partially amended as follows:
In Article 9-7 (2) 1, “Article 45 of the Water Leisure Safety Act” is replaced with “Article 43 of the Water Leisure Safety Act”.
(6) The Act on the Use and Management of Beaches is partially amended as follows:
In Article 26 (1), “persons using water leisure craft under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Water Leisure Safety Act and Article 39 (1) of that Act” is replaced with “persons using water leisure craft under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Water Leisure Safety Act and Article 37 (1) of that Act”.

Article 23 (Relationship with Other Statutes and Regulations)
Where another statute or regulation cites the former Water Leisure Safety Act or a provision thereof as at the time this Act enters into force, and this Act contains a corresponding provision, that citation shall be deemed a citation of this Act or the relevant provision of this Act in place of the former provision.

ADDENDA (Maritime Traffic Safety Act) <Act No. 19573, July 25, 2023>
